title: Aquarium Deep Systems Sprint
specification:
# Aquarium Deep Systems Sprint

This PRD is intentionally lane-pure. PM should decompose it into a large aquarium-only sprint for `aquarium-agent`.

## Product Goal

Turn aquarium from a compact prototype into a deeper management loop with visible mid-run progression, more expressive fish behavior, stronger threat escalation, and clearer player-facing goals.

The player experience should move from:

- feed fish
- collect coins
- react to pests

to a richer loop with:

- short-term tank maintenance decisions
- medium-term roster and upgrade planning
- escalating danger waves
- clearer win / loss pressure and session milestones

## Sprint Shape

PM should plan a large sprint, not a smoke test.

Expected shape:

- 10 to 14 implementation tasks
- all tasks assigned to `aquarium-agent`
- one shared aquarium lane branch
- one aquarium PR with many commits
- no cross-lane work

Each task should be small enough for one commit, but together they should add up to a meaningful feature sprint.

## Scope Boundaries

Stay inside:

- `src/barebones-starter/games/apps/aquarium/**`

Primary files and folders likely to matter:

- `config.ts`
- `world.ts`
- `step.ts`
- `draw.ts`
- `constants.ts`
- `types.ts`
- `actors/**`
- `logic/**`
- `sprites.ts`
- aquarium-local docs or sprint notes if needed

## Deliverable Themes

PM should cover most of these themes in the task plan.

### 1. Run Progression and Goals

- add clearer stage goals or milestone targets
- make success / failure pressure legible over a longer session
- introduce mid-run pacing beats so the tank evolves over time

### 2. Fish Roster Depth

- create more distinct fish archetypes and upgrade paths
- strengthen fish personality differences in movement, appetite, output, or upkeep
- make the roster feel intentionally tiered rather than flat

### 3. Economy and Upgrade Loop

- deepen coin generation and spending choices
- make upgrades feel synergistic rather than isolated
- improve recovery options after weak play without removing risk

### 4. Threat Director

- improve pest escalation and wave logic
- introduce at least one more dramatic threat beat such as miniboss pressure, special pest types, or timed danger windows
- make defensive tools and their tradeoffs clearer

### 5. Presentation and Readability

- improve HUD clarity
- make important state changes visible in moment-to-moment play
- improve animation / visual feedback / sprite usage where practical

### 6. Session Wrap-Up

- improve end-of-run clarity, summaries, or milestone messaging
- leave the player with a sense of what advanced during the session

## Planning Rules For PM

- Do not emit tasks for other agents.
- Do not emit reviewer tasks.
- Prefer tasks that change real gameplay or presentation systems over placeholder markdown notes.
- Prefer modifying existing aquarium systems over adding throwaway scaffolding.
- Spread the plan across multiple aquarium subsystems so the sprint naturally creates many commits.
- Include tests only where the repo already supports them naturally for the touched area.

## Definition Of Done

- Aquarium has a visibly deeper progression loop.
- The tank feels more alive, more pressured, and more readable than the current baseline.
- The sprint touches multiple aquarium subsystems, not just tuning constants.
- The resulting PR should plausibly contain many commits because the work decomposes into many real tasks.

## Explicit Non-Goals

- no changes outside aquarium scope
- no generic placeholder files just to inflate task count
- no PM-generated reviewer work
requirements: Produce between 10 and 14 implementation tasks total.
Assign every implementation task to aquarium-agent only.
Do not create tasks for adventure-agent
Keep every task scoped to files under src/barebones-starter/games/apps/aquarium/ only.
Tasks must be atomic enough to land as one commit each on the shared aquarium lane branch.
The resulting implementation should feel like one large aquarium sprint rather than isolated note files.
The reviewer should merge one aquarium PR after the lane finishes all tasks.

tasks.title: Add stage progression and run-state pressure
tasks.description: Introduce stage progression data, milestone targets, and run-status tracking so aquarium sessions advance through explicit beats instead of a flat endless loop.
acceptance: State initialization seeds stage 1 with explicit goal and timeout data and stores run status in aquarium state.
During play, meeting a stage target advances stage data and emits a stage-transition message without resetting fish or economy state.
Failing a stage timer or losing all fish flips run status to a non-active state that aquarium rendering can read.

tasks.title: Render goals, countdowns, and warning banners
tasks.description: Expose active goals, stage countdowns, and urgent tank warnings in the aquarium HUD for both compact and standard layouts.
acceptance: The HUD shows the current stage name, goal progress, and remaining time or pressure in both compact and full-width layouts.
Incoming-wave, low-fish, or deadline-pressure states render with stronger visual treatment than normal shop chrome.
Aquarium messages are rendered on-screen as a readable banner or panel instead of existing only in state.

tasks.title: Retune the fish roster into distinct tiers
tasks.description: Give each shop fish explicit role stats and unlock tiers so buying fish becomes a medium-term roster planning choice.
acceptance: Every shop fish type has distinct price, appetite, income cadence or value, and role data instead of sharing one default profile.
At least two roster tiers exist, with higher-tier fish locked until the player reaches the intended stage or milestone.
Shop purchasing and fish spawning use per-species data and preserve those stats on created fish entities.

tasks.title: Add mid-run fish growth paths
tasks.description: Implement fish growth or promotion breakpoints tied to feeding and survival so existing fish visibly improve over a session.
acceptance: Fish accumulate progression toward at least one higher-value growth breakpoint during normal play.
Crossing a breakpoint changes a fish's visible stage or badge and improves output or survivability without replacing it with a new purchase.
Growth progress persists across simulation steps and is available to later HUD or summary systems.

tasks.title: Differentiate fish behavior and state cues
tasks.description: Deepen fish AI with role-specific movement and readable cues so the tank feels more alive and players can see who needs attention.
acceptance: At least three behavior signatures are observable across the roster, such as grazing, darting, schooling, resting, or threat-avoidance.
Fish react differently to food and pests based on their role stats instead of all sharing the same chase loop.
Hungry, injured, or especially productive fish display an in-world cue through animation, tint, or iconography.

tasks.title: Add water-quality maintenance pressure
tasks.description: Introduce a tank maintenance system that turns overfeeding and neglect into a short-term management problem with real penalties.
acceptance: Aquarium state includes a maintenance meter with at least safe, warning, and critical bands and updates it every run.
Warning and critical maintenance bands measurably reduce fish performance or increase danger when ignored.
The current maintenance band and critical alerts are visible to the player during play.

tasks.title: Replace the utility placeholder with recovery actions
tasks.description: Turn the existing potion or utility slot into a real comeback tool, such as cleanup, emergency healing, or a temporary stability buff.
acceptance: Pressing the utility slot performs a concrete recovery action instead of showing placeholder text.
The recovery action costs coins and includes a clear tradeoff such as cooldown, capped effect, or lower efficiency than proactive upkeep.
The action can rescue a weak run from warning state without fully erasing repeated mistakes.

tasks.title: Rebalance economy and upgrade synergies
tasks.description: Tune coin flow, pellet spend, passive pickup, and upgrade scaling so feeding, fish growth, maintenance, and recovery systems create real spending choices.
acceptance: Default balance still allows pellet purchases from the opening state and makes at least one upgrade or new fish reachable before stage 3 under normal coin collection.
Food-strength and drop-speed upgrades modify a growth-facing or maintenance-facing effect in addition to their direct stat bump.
Passive coin expiry payout and utility costs are tuned so a weak run can still recover with deliberate play while unattended play can still stall or collapse.

tasks.title: Enable a live pest director
tasks.description: Turn pests back on and drive wave cadence from stage progression and tank pressure rather than a disabled flat timer.
acceptance: With default aquarium balance, pests spawn during a normal run without manual constant edits.
Next-wave size, timing, or composition respond to stage or pressure data instead of only the old fixed timer.
Wave telegraph state and spawn timers reset cleanly after each wave and when the run ends.

tasks.title: Add a special threat beat
tasks.description: Introduce a more dramatic enemy moment with at least one special pest or miniboss that creates a distinct mid-run danger spike.
acceptance: A special threat type appears from a defined stage or wave trigger rather than random baseline spawns.
The special threat is visually distinguishable and uses attack or movement behavior that baseline pests do not share.
Defeating the special threat grants a distinct reward or clears a specific pressure effect.

tasks.title: Add a purchasable defensive tool
tasks.description: Restore active defense depth with a bought-and-placed turret or equivalent tool that supplements tap combat and forces an economic tradeoff.
acceptance: The aquarium HUD or shop exposes a defense purchase flow and the player can place the defense inside the tank via aquarium-local input handling.
Placed defenses automatically engage pests and use the existing projectile or collision loop.
Defense spending competes with fish and upgrades by costing enough or consuming a slot or limit, so it is not a free add-on.

tasks.title: Add end-of-run states and a session summary
tasks.description: Define clear win and loss outcomes and present a run-wrap overlay that explains what the player achieved before restarting.
acceptance: Aquarium enters a visible failure state when all fish are lost or stage pressure collapses, and a visible success state when the capstone milestone is reached.
The wrap-up UI lists stage reached, coins earned, fish lost or grown, and the most important upgrades or utilities used.
Restarting from the wrap-up recreates the initial aquarium state cleanly without touching non-aquarium code.
